quotes.text: In directory terms, the source of authority determines which system has final say over an object's identity attributes.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concise definition of the episode's core concept.

quotes.text: Running two authoritative systems is like maintaining two versions of reality. You'll never be entirely sure who a user truly is at any given moment.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains vividly why dual sources of authority undermine identity security.

quotes.text: When you flip an object to cloud management, Entra will treat that data as canonical truth. Garbage in becomes garbage immortalized.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the case for cleaning directory data before migration.

quotes.text: The most common administrative blunder at this stage is skipping the verification step. Patch first, assume success later. That's how authentication collapses midday.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A practical warning about verifying each source of authority change.

takeaways: The source of authority decides which directory owns an object's attributes, and dual control between Active Directory and Entra ID causes sync drift, lockouts and inconsistent policies.
Clean up duplicates and sync scope, enforce modern MFA and document Entra Connect configuration before flipping isCloudManaged on any object.
Migrate groups first, then pilot users, verify every change via Graph and sign-in logs, and then use access reviews, Conditional Access and lifecycle workflows to govern from the cloud.
hook: Running Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID side by side means double policies, sync drift and broken logins. This episode is for identity admins planning a move to cloud-managed identities. It shows how to shift the source of authority for groups and users step by step without breaking authentication.
